dedupe_keys.name: land neutral expansion of brazilian renewable fuel production spatio temporal model of methanol from ethanol refinery co2 and renewable hydrogen boku and chalmers

description: This Zenodo record holds the code and data for the paper Pathway to a land-neutral expansion of Brazilian renewable fuel production, by Luis Ramirez Camargo and colleagues at the University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna, with Jessica Jewell of Chalmers University of Technology. The paper proposes raising output from ethanol refineries by combining surplus CO2 from fermentation with hydrogen from renewably powered electrolysis to make methanol, and illustrates it with a spatio-temporal model of the Brazilian sugarcane ethanol industry. Abstract results: existing plants could raise fuel output by 43 to 49 percent, or 100 TWh, without more land; wind needs the least land while a wind and solar mix costs least; and in the cheapest scenario green methanol matches fossil methanol at about 95 euro per tonne of CO2. The deposit is a 1.4 GB zip with a how-to PDF describing the data and how to install and run the simulation; it is free under CC BY 4.0 and dates from April 2022. Coverage is Brazil. Caveats: the language and solver are not stated on the record page and the PDF could not be read here. Simulation uses are siting and sizing renewable power and electrolysis at refinery sites for fuel supply planning. Related records: data-enerdata-hydrogen-derivatives-projects-database tracks methanol and e-fuel projects.
